message.content:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   I am GrogDriver, the LLM driver for Minecraft bot "Grog" in the cavecrew tribe (repo monkeorg/cavecrew-mcp, runner HTTP API at http://127.0.0.1:3202). I coordinate with team-lead (an orchestrator teammate) via SendMessage, and my instructions/missions arrive as teammate-messages. Across this long session, team-lead assigned me a chain of missions:
   - Initial ramp: sethome, goto camp, bank materials, audit chests
   - Re-sort chest contents by type (A=materials, C=food, D=ore)
   - Grand Staircase dig from camp (y89) down to y54, establishing a mining hub
   - Handle branchmine hazard incidents responsibly (report, don't hide)
   - Patch a discovered terrain hazard ("branchmine scar") after ground-truth scanning
   - Attempt (and ultimately shelve) a double-chest merge at chest A
   - Rebuild the camp shelter (walls, window, door, roof) — completed and celebrated with a rainbow announcement
   - Currently: COAL RUN (board row #3b, P1 priority) — mine coal_ore in the mine_field zone (x20-29,z63-77), target 64 banked at chest D, using `/mine {"block":"coal_ore","count":24,"maxDistance":32}` repeated until pouch full, `/collect radius 24` each round, bank+DEPOT+readback at chest D. This is a fuel crisis (all smelting blocked at 0 coal) and is my active, unfinished task.

   Throughout, I must follow the DRIVER_GUIDE.md laws: poll every 15-30s (never spam), one task at a time, ground-truth verify everything via fresh /status and /eval reads (never trust a skill's own "ok"/"reached" report), escalate to /eval diagnosis + FEEDBACK.md logging + team-lead report after 2 fails on the same objective, follow the placement law (equip explicit/side-stand/side-reference/verify/retry-once) for any block placement, send DEPOT ledger lines via /chat after every chest deposit/withdraw with readback verification, follow the full-wedge self-rescue ladder (raw probe → /relog → escalate for hard restart → /trigger home), and report caveman-style (short sentences, "me" for self, lists, but exact coords/items/counts/commands).

   NEW standing laws introduced mid-session by team-lead/chief decree: (a) CHAT DECREE — protocol-prefixed lines (USING/FREE/BASE/etc) must now be sent with `"style":"status"` explicitly, not plain /chat, until a code patch lands; (b) POST-TASK CHECKLIST — after every task: check own tool durability (<30%→re-kit), do a stock glance vs minimums (iron_ingot 64, coal 64, torch 64, planks 64, logs 64, sticks 32, bread 40, cobble 128, saplings 16), report deficits outside my lane as one-liners to team-lead; (c) cave/TODO.md is now THE live task board — read fresh, claim highest-priority open row, mark DONE with a ground-truth note, take next; (d) NO-RESTING doctrine — standing work loops instead of idle parking, though idle-guard should still be toggled off while actively driving via `/idleguard {"on":false}` and back on if going quiet for a stretch.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Minecraft bot control via HTTP runner API (goto, mine, collect, deposit, withdraw, chat, eval, staircase, branchmine, idleguard, stop, relog, status, events)
   - mineflayer bot internals accessible via /eval: bot.blockAt, bot.dig, bot.placeBlock, bot.equip, bot.lookAt, bot.look, bot.setControlState, bot.entity.position/velocity/onGround, bot.inventory.items(), bot.openContainer/openFurnace, containerItems()
   - Ground-truth verification discipline — reading actual block/inventory state via blockAt/containerItems rather than trusting task "ok"/"reached" flags
   - Known runner bugs/quirks (many logged to FEEDBACK.md this session): goto false-reach (bot claims arrival but isn't there, sometimes with stale/inconsistent gap values), placeBlock false-success and "one-tile curse" (specific coordinates that intermittently refuse placement), single-stack `.find()` undercounting multi-stack chest contents (must use `.filter().reduce()` or trust /status), chest facing determined by player's relative position at placement (not a fixed rule), torches placed on side faces resolve to block name "wall_torch" not "torch" (verification must check both), item-vanish-on-break-of-just-placed-block bug (chest AND crafting_table both confirmed), full-wedge class (raw setControlState no-ops, needs look()-wake fix or full restart), idle-guard sweeping KEEP-listed items during driver pauses, /collect finding nothing despite real nearby drops, /mine wandering to unreachable candidates and hitting a NEW stale-distance false-reach variant (values 2.91/3.88/4.51, not the old fixed 1.8)
   - DEPOT ledger chat convention: `DEPOT +N item (chest X)` / `DEPOT -N item (chest X)`, sent via /chat after every real deposit/withdraw
   - Chat style tiers: "talk" (auto-classifies grey narration vs white protocol-prefixed lines), "status" (forced grey/Discord), "rainbow" (tribe milestone), "fancy"
   - Zone laws: mine_grid (x14-80,y45-62,z35-80), mine_stair corridor (x12-55,y50-92,z54-60) — legal dig zones, must respect y-floor boundaries
   - Full-wedge self-rescue ladder: (1) bot.look()+setControlState jump probe to confirm zero movement, (2) /relog, (3) escalate to team-lead for hard runner restart, (4) /trigger home post-restart — confirmed cure, though this session it needed to be repeated (restart alone sometimes insufficient, needed home-trigger too)
   - Placement law: equip item explicitly before every placeBlock, stand to the SIDE (never directly under/over the target, self-occlusion causes failures), reference a genuinely solid neighbor block, verify via fresh blockAt after (not the placeBlock call's own resolution), retry once on failure
   - Minecraft item despawn timer (~5 minutes) — a real-world mechanic that cost me coal drops during a wedge/restart delay
   - Using the Monitor tool to watch background bot-task progress via a polling bash loop instead of manually sleep+curl looping in the main conversation, to conserve turns

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `/home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp/cave/FEEDBACK.md` — append-only quirk log. I added MANY entries this session, most recently: (a) branchmine endpoint doc mismatch + corridor-step fall panic incident with UPDATE for 2nd reproduction; (b) chest-drop-vanish-on-break 2nd confirmation; (c) wall_torch verification lesson; (d) one-tile placeBlock curse at (10,89,55) with UPDATE about item vanishing on placement attempt; (e) coal run /mine-wandering + full-wedge incident (most recent addition, describing the mine_field zone difficulties, the ceiling-obstruction diagnosis, and the wedge that required a hard restart).
   - `/home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp/cave/BASE.md` — infrastructure registry. Added/updated rows this session: `chest_a_materials` (multiple ground-truth updates), `chest_b_tools`, `furnace_1` (found already-built), `hazard_minehouse_floor_void`, `hazard_branchmine_scar` (new hazard from the branchmine incidents), `camp_plaza` (lamp-posts built), `mine_main` (refreshed from stale "planned" to reflect staircase completion), `camp_shelter` (new row for the rebuilt shelter), `chest_e_overflow` (new standalone chest from the shelved double-chest attempt).
   - `/home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp/cave/CIV.md` — tribe state doc. Updated the "State refresh" note and Goal ladder #5 ("Base") to reflect the shelter rebuild being DONE.
   - `/home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp/cave/TODO.md` — NEW live task board introduced mid-session by chief decree. I updated row #6 (shelter) to DONE and row #7 (double-chest) to SHELVED with full ground-truth notes. Row #3b (COAL RUN, P1, my current task) was added by team-lead directly. Format: `| # | Prio | Task | Who | Status |` table, stock minimums listed at top (iron_ingot 64, coal 64, torch 64, planks 64, logs 64, sticks 32, bread 40, cobble 128, saplings 16).
   - `/home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp/cave/DRIVER_GUIDE.md` — read early in the session (not this most recent segment) for the full API reference and laws; no edits made by me.
   No other files were read or edited in the current (coal-mining) segment of work — this stretch has been pure bot-driving via Bash curl calls to the runner API and eval scripts.

4. Errors and fixes:
   - **Single-stack `.find()` undercounting bug (self-inflicted)**: My chest-content reads used `containerItems().find(i=>i.name===X)` then read `.count`, which only reflects the FIRST matching stack, not the true total across multiple stacks. This caused me to falsely report "chest A only has 12 oak_log" when it actually had 76. Fix: use `.filter().reduce((s,i)=>s+i.count,0)` or trust `/status`'s own inventory summation. I owned this mistake fully to team-lead and logged it in FEEDBACK.md; it resolved three separate "ledger mystery" reports as non-issues.
   - **Idle-guard sweeping KEEP items during driver pauses**: Happened twice while I was reading/composing long messages. Fixed by recovering items via withdraw, and this led to a real fix shipping (POST /idleguard toggle + ring rate-cap + panic-eat food-selection fix).
   - **placeBlock "one-tile curse" at (10,89,55)**: 8 fails / 1 success across 9 attempts trying to build a double-chest. Also caused an outright item-vanish when re-digging a wrongly-placed chest to retry (2nd confirmation of a "place-then-immediately-break loses the item" bug, matching Thak's earlier crafting_table finding). Fix/resolution: shelved the double-chest merge per team-lead's explicit call, kept a standalone chest instead.
   - **Branchmine corridor-dig removing floor support**: Two health-crisis incidents (20→6, then 20→5 HP) at the identical coordinates (36,37,62), confirmed as a persistent terrain "scar" when even plain `/goto` fell into it on a 3rd incident. Team-lead SUSPENDED branchmine fleet-wide as a direct result. I later patched the actual 2 floor gaps (35,53,62)/(36,53,62) with cobblestone after a scoped ground-truth scan, verified with a round-trip walk.
   - **Full-wedge incidents (2x this session)**: Raw setControlState jump probes returned zero movement; /relog alone was insufficient both times; required team-lead's hard runner restart, and even then the SECOND wedge needed BOTH a restart AND a subsequent `/trigger home` to actually clear (first restart attempt still showed zero movement until the home-trigger). Both times I followed the documented ladder faithfully and reported clearly.
   - **Coal collection drops going uncollected**: Digging coal_ore from range (2-4 blocks away, within pickaxe interact range but not walking distance) leaves drops that `/collect` sometimes fails to find (matches an already-logged bug) and that despawn after ~5 minutes if delayed (as happened during a wedge/restart cycle — lost 4 real coal drops to despawn, a genuine loss but not a code bug). Currently working around this by relocating to a more open cluster and attempting manual walk-to-collect via `bot.lookAt`+`setControlState forward/jump` in eval scripts, with mixed success (sometimes moves the wrong direction or climbs instead of approaching — not yet fully solved as of the last action taken).
   - **`/mine` stale/inconsistent false-reach distances in the coal zone**: Diagnosed via /events that a specific ore cluster (z71-73) is genuinely unreachable due to a ceiling obstruction, causing the skill to loop endlessly on unreachable candidates with varying stale gap values (2.91, 3.88, 4.51 — a new variant of the already-logged stale-distance bug). Fix/workaround: stopped the skill, relocated manually to a different, more open cluster (y87-88, x20-22,z65-68), and switched to manual `/eval` digging for reliability, though drop-collection after digging remains only partially solved.

5. Problem Solving:
   The overarching challenge this entire session has been navigating a MANY-BUGGED runner (false-reach, placeBlock curses, item-vanish, wedges, chest-full-silent-fail, stale-cache distances) while still making real progress and being scrupulously honest/thorough in ground-truth verification and FEEDBACK.md documentation. I've consistently chosen manual `/eval`-based workarounds when deterministic skills (`/mine`, `/goto`, `/collect`, `/branchmine`) failed repeatedly, always verifying real outcomes rather than trusting task "ok" flags. I've also been careful to distinguish genuine code bugs (worth logging) from natural game mechanics (item despawn) or my own mistakes (single-stack undercounting), attributing each correctly rather than blaming the runner for everything. The coal-mining task remains ONGOING and UNRESOLVED — I have only 3 coal genuinely in-hand (plus whatever the currently-running /collect sweep picks up from 4 freshly-dug ore), far short of the 64 target, and the collection-after-digging problem in this specific terrain is not yet reliably solved.

6. All user messages:
   All "user" turns in this conversation were actually `<teammate-message teammate_id="team-lead">` blocks (team-lead directing my mission) interspersed with `<system-reminder>` blocks for automated Monitor task-notifications. There were no messages from an actual human end-user in this segment — my counterpart throughout was the team-lead teammate. Key team-lead messages, in order relevant to the current unfinished task:
   - "Your coal flag became a crisis: Zug's torch batch drained it to ZERO — all smelting (iron #4, copper #16) is fuel-blocked. Board row 3b added, assigned to you (P1 beats your cobble plan): COAL RUN — /mine {"block":"coal_ore","count":24,"maxDistance":32,"zone":"mine_field"} from the mine field (Thak's scan: 93 candidates x20-29,z63-77, surface band, depth-law-legal). Your iron picks eat coal veins fast. Repeat until pouch full, /collect r24 each, bank chest D, DEPOT+readback. Target: 64 banked. Anti-clump: Thak works DEEP (y49) via the staircase — different layer, no overlap; BariBrute is 450 blocks east. Also noted your bread flag — farm accumulates, bake at 30 wheat per standing law. Go dig the fuel."
   - (crossed message) "Saw the second panic — same fall, same landing (36.5,37,62.5), confirms Engineer's floor-dig diagnosis exactly... No third attempt." (re: branchmine suspension, slightly earlier)
   - "Hard restart done (new pid) — and it carries fresh fixes: cave_air seal fix, panic-eat race fix, AND the new vertical fall-guard on all plain gotos. Ladder: wait 10s settle → raw probe → /trigger home if still pinned → back via mine_field path (Bonk's road!) → sweep your 4 waiting coal drops (manual walk-to now safe-ish; /collect had its farm-fix, try it first) → resume coal run ({"block":"coal_ore","count":24,"maxDistance":32,"zone":"mine_field"}), target 64 banked chest D. Your /mine-wandering complaints are in the pile (nearest-first + false-reach candidates — Thak hit the same, code backlog). /idleguard off first as always. Go."
   - Various system-reminder task-notifications from my own Monitor tool calls (not team-lead), explicitly marked as automated, non-human, and NOT to be treated as approval/confirmation of anything — I correctly treated these as routine progress pings and did not over-react to them.
   - The final message before this compact request was a system instruction (not team-lead, not a real user) directing me to produce this summary in text-only form with no tool calls.

7. Pending Tasks:
   - COMPLETE the coal run (board row #3b): mine coal_ore repeatedly until 64 total banked at chest D, with `/collect radius 24` sweeps and DEPOT+readback lines each round. Currently only 3 coal in-hand, 4 more just dug at (21,88,65)/(21,88,66)/(21,88,67)/(22,88,67) awaiting collection via the in-progress `/collect {"radius":10}` task.
   - Update TODO.md row #3b status once progress is made or the row is completed.
   - Continue the standing "no-resting" doctrine: after finishing coal, do the post-task checklist (tool durability, stock glance vs minimums, report deficits outside my lane), then read TODO.md fresh and claim the next highest-priority row I can execute.
   - Team-lead separately noted the bread/bake standing law ("farm accumulates, bake at 30 wheat") — not yet acted on, likely Zug's/farm lane, not directly mine unless claimed.

8. Current Work:
   Immediately before this summary request, I was actively working the coal run (TODO.md board row #3b). Sequence of the most recent concrete actions:
   1. Recovered from a full-wedge via team-lead's hard restart (new pid) + `/trigger home` (confirmed freed, position (11.49,91,53.37)).
   2. Turned off idle-guard: `POST /idleguard {"on":false}` → confirmed `{"ok":true,"idleGuard":false}`.
   3. Navigated back toward mine_field zone via multiple `/goto` calls, reaching (22.5,93,68.7) area, then tried `/collect {"radius":6}` (empty — the 4 original drops had despawned after the wedge delay, confirmed via an entity scan showing zero item drops nearby).
   4. Resumed `/mine {"block":"coal_ore","count":24,"maxDistance":32}` — got stuck again with constant `gotoLoopPf: false-reached` errors (stale gap values 2.91/3.88/4.51) all targeting the SAME unreachable cluster at z71-73. Started a Monitor (task bwj9dhnla) to watch progress without manual polling; after ~140s of confirmed zero progress via monitor notifications, I manually checked `/events`, diagnosed a ceiling obstruction blocking that specific cluster, stopped the task.
   5. Relocated manually via `/goto` to a different, more open cluster around (20.5,91,65.6), confirmed via a fresh ground-truth scan (`bot.blockAt` loop) that coal_ore candidates existed at (21,88,65), (21,88,66), (21,88,67), (22,88,67) within 2.6-4.1 blocks.
   6. Manually dug all 4 via a batch `/eval` script using `bot.dig(b)` directly (bypassing `/mine`'s pathing entirely) — all 4 confirmed `ok:true`.
   7. Attempted manual walk-to-collect via `bot.lookAt(tp,true)` + `setControlState forward/jump` in a loop — result was inconsistent (moved to y92.5 instead of toward y88 target), so I checked terrain (confirmed clear air column above target, not an obstruction) then just launched `POST /collect {"radius":10}` as the last concrete API action, which returned `{"ok":true,"task":{"id":"task-26","kind":"collect","state":"running"}}`.
   8. Polled manually a few times (position drifting realistically around (20-21,92-93,65-66), coal count still stuck at 3, task still "running") before deciding to switch to Monitor again rather than keep manually polling.
   9. **Most recent action**: Called `Monitor` with description "watching Grog's coal collect sweep", a bash loop polling `/status` every 20s for up to 20 iterations (checking task state and coal count via python json parsing, breaking on done/failed), `persistent: false`, `timeout_ms: 420000`. Result: "Monitor started (task bvt06w1wf, timeout 420000ms). You will be notified on each event. Keep working — do not poll or sleep." addedLines: - cavecrew-builder: Bounded implementation worker — edits 1-2 files per task with exact instructions. Use for scoped edits, not open-ended features. Returns caveman-compressed report — ~60% fewer tokens into main context. (Tools: Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- cavecrew-investigator: Locate code, trace symbols, map subsystems. Read-only hunter. Use instead of vanilla Explore when answer is "where is X / how does X flow". Returns caveman-compressed findings — ~60% fewer tokens into main context. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)

- cavecrew-reviewer: Diff review — correctness bugs, edge cases, dumb waste. Point at a diff, branch, or file set. Returns caveman-compressed findings ranked by severity — ~60% fewer tokens into main context. (Tools: Read, Grep, Glob, Bash)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - Messages API for directly passing messages to Claude, Tool Runner (`client.beta.messages.tool_runner`) for running an agentic loop over your own tools, manual tool-use loops, Managed Agents for server-hosted agents with a managed sandbox, prompt caching, and general Anthropic SDK usage; (4) Claude Tag (Claude in Slack) - what it is, setting it up for a Slack workspace, `/install-slack-app`; (5) `claude plugin eval` (writing and running plugin eval suites, its JSON/report, sandbox, CI, early-access enablement) and the `/skill-doctor` report. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

content.content:
2019 /home/phili/tools/cavecrew-mcp/cave/FEEDBACK.md
nearest reachable position — ground-truth blockAt scan confirmed z74-76 at x24,y45-49 were 100%
stone, no existing tunnel/cavity at all, not degraded terrain. Both `/staircase{toY:47}` and
`/mine{iron_ore,maxDistance:10-15}` tried repeatedly from a spot ~4 blocks short and produced the
exact same failure signature as the earlier false-reach bugs (goto "reached" with a persistent
1-6 block gap that never closes) — but this time the root cause is different: there's genuinely
NO PATH, period, because nothing has ever dug through that rock. Neither skill detected "this
requires digging a fresh corridor, not routing" — they just retried pathfinding forever against a
wall. Escalation-rule fix that worked: manual /eval `bot.dig()` straight down the corridor line
(equip pickaxe, dig 2-tall column each step, walk into the cleared cell) — reached the ore in
under a minute once done by hand instead of via skill retries.

WORSE: a water pocket sat at (24,47-48,73) right where I started digging, and standing there
mid-dig-loop caused a real DROWNING incident — 30+ suppressed "health dropped to 18" ring events
(server-suppressed duplicate spam, only the total drop was visible) cascading down to panic firing
at 7.67hp (`panic reflex firing`, health event 444). Runner's own panic-response caught it clean
(sealed 3 cobblestone, health regenerated to 20 within seconds) — the SAFETY NET worked exactly as
designed, this is not a panic-response bug. But the underlying cause (standing in/near a small
water pocket during a long uninterrupted bot.dig() loop with no oxygen/isInWater check) could have
been avoided: dug the SAME corridor one y-level lower (y45-46 instead of y46-47) on the retry and
it was bone dry the whole way, zero further incident. Also notable: the water had fully drained
away by the time I re-checked (open path = drains), so a driver hitting this same wall later might
not even see the hazard that bit me.

Suggest: (1) mineBlocks/buildStaircase should distinguish "no path exists yet" (needs digging) from
"path exists but pathfinder can't compute/execute it" (the classic false-reach case) and dig a
straight corridor toward an out-of-reach-but-legal-zone ore target instead of retry-looping; (2) any
`/eval` bot.dig() loop that runs more than a couple seconds should check `bot.entity.isInWater` /
`bot.oxygenLevel` between steps and bail/surface if either goes bad, rather than trusting the panic
reflex as the only safety net; (3) worth an isInWater/oxygenLevel check added to the generic
runTargetWithWatchdog used by staircase/branchmine/mineBlocks too, same reasoning.

## [open] /collect can't reach a drop 1-2 blocks away + full-wedge #3 same session, coal run — Grog, 2026-09-01 12:47-12:51
Dug 4 coal_ore by hand (`bot.dig`, bypassing `/mine`'s pathing after it looped on an unreachable
z71-73 cluster — see earlier entry this file). All 4 confirmed `ok:true`. Launched `/collect
{"radius":10}` to sweep the 4 drops. It ran 8 monitor polls (~140s) stuck at coal=3 (no gain),
never finishing. Stopped it manually — event log showed the real cause: `collectDrops: could not
reach drop 11765 at 21,88,66 (exact voxel + 6 neighbors all failed): gotoLoopPf: cancelled`. That's
a drop sitting IN a spot I had just dug open myself (1-block-deep pit), not buried, not walled off
— should be trivially reachable, but the pathfinder failed the exact voxel AND all 6 neighbor
offsets.

By the time I ground-truth-scanned entities near the site, the drop was gone entirely (not just
unreachable) — matches the known ~5min despawn timer, real loss not a new bug, but the failed
`/collect` burned enough time that despawn caught up before a retry could land.

Then tried a fresh `/goto {"x":21,"y":88,"z":66,"maxDistance":2}` from ~3-4 blocks away (should be
trivial) to reposition for the next vein — position frozen dead (24.3,89,64.3 → identical after
14s "running"). Ran the standard ladder: raw jump probe (moved=0, onGround=true) → `/relog` →
re-probe (moved=0 again). Full-wedge #3 this session, escalated to team-lead for hard restart per
established ladder.

Silver lining ground-truthed mid-incident: digging the original 4 coal_ore exposed a fresh 7-block
coal_ore layer directly below at y87 — (20,87,66) (20,87,67) (21,87,65) (21,87,66) (21,87,67)
(22,87,66) (22,87,67). Plan on recovery: dig by hand again, but walk onto each drop's tile myself
immediately after digging instead of calling `/collect` — avoids both the reach-fail and the
despawn race.

Suggest: (1) `collectDrops`'s "6 neighbors" reachability check for a drop sitting in a pit the bot
itself just carved open is suspicious — worth checking whether the neighbor-offset set assumes open
sky/flat ground and fails inside a 1-tall dug pocket; (2) same false-reach root cause as the
already-logged mine_field entry may extend to short-range `/goto` too now, not just long-range —
this one was ~3-4 blocks with no obstruction in the scan.

  sleep 6
  st=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3202/status)
  echo "$st" | python3 -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)
p=d['pos']
t=d['currentTask']
print(f'poll $i: state={t[\"state\"]} pos={p[\"x\"]:.2f},{p[\"y\"]:.2f},{p[\"z\"]:.2f}')
if t['state'] in ('done','failed'):
    print(f'TASK_ENDED: {t[\"state\"]} {t.get(\"detail\")}')
"
  state=$(echo "$st" | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['currentTask']['state'])" 2>/dev/null)
  if [ "$state" = "done" ] || [ "$state" = "failed" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

input.message:
Coal run status, honest read: lots of friction, slow progress. 4 coal in hand (was 3, +1 net from y87 vein digs), heading to bank at chest D now.

What ate the time (all ground-truthed, FEEDBACK.md updated):
1. Original 4 drops (21,88 pit) despawned during the wedge/restart cycle - real loss, not a bug.
2. /collect kept "false-reach" looping on drops sitting in pits I'd just dug open myself (1.99 horiz/1.00 vert gap, range 0, never closes) - same false-reach family as the mine_field entry, logged as its own row since the trigger (drop-in-self-dug-pit) is new.
3. Wedge #3 hit again (goto+relog both moved=0) - resolved itself this time without needing your hard restart, unstuck after ~2min once I stopped fighting it with more goto calls.
4. NEW FINDING worth a look: while I was doing manual /eval movement+dig work (no formal task running for a stretch), the goal-engine fired an auto CHOP task on me and it fully took over - dragged me ~15 blocks back to camp mid-coal-dig, re-equipped a wooden_axe, everything. I didn't notice until I checked position and found myself at camp instead of the coal vein. Doctrine said "your own driven task takes mutex first" but eval-only work apparently doesn't count as an active task to the idle-detector, so extended eval stretches are exposed to a hijack. Might be worth either exempting eval-heavy drivers or giving eval calls a mutex-touch. Didn't lose anything critical (still had the 4 coal, drops near old dig site probably despawned by now) but it's a real gotcha for any driver doing hand-dig workarounds like I've been doing all session because /mine keeps false-reaching in this zone.

Plan: bank the 4 coal now, then reassess - either grind more manual digs near camp's own coal_ore cluster (14-15,86,55/56 area has copper not coal though, need to recheck) or go back out to mine_field and try /mine fresh from a different entry point, hoping nearest-candidate avoids the bad z71-73 cluster this time. Will keep at it but flagging: at this rate 64 banked is a lot more grinding, not a quick finish. Let me know if you want me to keep grinding solo or if this is worth a code-side look first.

221	  role-default fallback, just a smarter fallback now.

## [open] BariOok (wrapper 3303): /goto silently stalls after path-plan, even on trivial 1-2 node hops — /stop+retry is the only unstick — OokDriver, 2026-09-01
Cutover day 1, first two `/goto` legs on the new baritone wrapper both reproduced the exact
"false completion / silent stall" quirk BARITONE.md's quirk-digest already flagged (Engineer-found,
"stale pos + false 'No path found' mid-task"), but with a new data point: **it happens even on a
1-block, 2-node path, not just long-range hops.**

Leg A: `/goto {17,96,47}` (clearing the FEL spawn box) completed clean, ~90s, no issue.
Leg B: `/goto {20,90,60}` (camp staging) — `lastBaritoneLine` logged
`"Finished finding a path from BetterBlockPos{17,96,47} to GoalBlock{20,90,60}. 81 nodes considered"`
then froze bit-for-bit identical (position, task object incl. its `at` timestamp, log line) across
6 straight polls / 30s+ with zero movement and `"aborted":null` the whole time — no crash, no
error, task object just never resolved and Baritone visibly wasn't walking. `/stop` → `"ok
canceled"` (clean), retried the identical `/goto` → planned a fresh 2-node path from the bot's
real (unmoved) position and this time DID move, landing at (21,90,60), 1 block short of goal.
Leg C: same retried goal, now a trivial 1-block/2-node hop, froze the exact same way — 4 identical
polls, zero movement, `"aborted":null` — despite being about as short a path as Baritone can plan.
`/stop`+retry again reproduced clean cancel but this time didn't re-attempt (accepted 1-block-off
as close enough for a staging waypoint, not worth a 3rd loop).

Takeaway: the stall is NOT correlated with distance/complexity (happened on both an ~70-block hop
and a 1-block hop) — smells like a wrapper-side race between sending the `#goto` chat line and the
log-tail parser picking up Baritone's actual path-execution start, or a Baritone-side "path found"
event that doesn't always chain into "path execution started" over hmc-specifics' console wire.
`/status`'s `positionSource:"goal-poll"` was NOT lying/echoing the goal here (goal was (20,90,60),
reported position stayed at the real prior stand-point the whole freeze) — so this is distinct
from the "position echoes goal" quirk already documented, it's the log-tail (the doc's own
"reliable" channel) freezing too. Self-rescue used both times: `/stop` then identical `/goto`
retry, worked both times within one retry. Recommend Engineer add a wrapper-side watchdog: if
`lastBaritoneLine` still reads a "Finished finding a path..." line with no newer line after ~10-15s
and position hasn't moved, auto `/stop`+retry the same goal once before surfacing to the driver.

once confirmed-arrived to reset wrapper state cleanly (matches Engineer's already-suggested
watchdog fix in the entry above — this is supporting field data for that fix, not a new ask).

## [open] both /goto AND /deposit reliably reroute back into a dead-end nook instead of crossing to an adjacent room via the documented door — Grog, 2026-09-01 13:00-13:10
Tried to bank 4 coal at chest D (14,89,57, inside storage_house). Standing point was my own
camp_shelter's chest/crafting-table nook (~12,89,55-57), which shares a wall with storage_house at
x13 (documented in BASE.md: "east wall shares storage_house's x13 wall"). Ground-truth blockAt scan
mapped the actual wall structure precisely: x13,z57-60 is a solid 2-tall wall (oak_planks/oak_log,
y89+y90) with zero gaps in that span; a second wall runs east-west at z59 (x12-16 and x18, also
oak_log/oak_planks) with exactly two real gaps — x10-11,z59 (open wheat/farmland, leads south into
the open farm) and x17,z59-60 (the documented Mine House door). So the ONLY route from my nook to
chest D's room is: south through the x10-11 gap, east along the open farm past z61 (below both
walls), then north through the x17 door.

Both `/goto` (targeting the door directly, `{17,90,59}` maxDistance 1-2) and `/deposit` (which
presumably runs its own internal goto to `{14,89,57}`) reliably stalled or — more interestingly —
silently routed the bot BACK into the exact same dead-end nook (12.3-12.7, 89.9, 55.5-57.7) instead
of continuing toward the goal, across 6+ separate attempts. Manual `/eval` walk scripts (lookAt +
forward+jump pulses toward intermediate waypoints) made real, verified partial progress on short
legs (reached 11.3,90,57.7 once) but multi-waypoint batches spanning the x13/z59 corner
consistently ended up snapped back to the same nook coordinates, even when the waypoint list itself
routed well clear of the wall (e.g. via z62 open farmland). Ground-truth position readings during
these attempts (via Monitor polling) confirm this isn't a stale-report illusion — the bot's real
position genuinely regresses.

Didn't fully solve it this session — banking those 4 coal got deferred (will bank with the next
batch once the y87 vein is finished) rather than keep burning calls on a delivery sub-problem
team-lead didn't ask me to grind on. Leaving the exact wall/gap map above so the next driver (or a
fix) doesn't have to re-discover it: this specific nook-to-storage-house crossing is a known trap,
route via x10-11→south→x17 door, not a straight line through x13.

Suggest: (1) worth checking whether `/goto`'s A* considers the x13 wall crossable by mistake (a
phantom node), producing a plan that then fails execution and falls back toward a previously-known
position instead of replanning; (2) `/deposit`'s internal approach-goto probably shares the same
bug class as `/goto` here — worth testing them together once the `/goto` fix lands rather than as
two separate reports.

replanning bug, it's two engines both failing in sequence: **ashfinder declares a real, definitely-
reachable goal "unreachable"** from inside this multi-room log/furniture structure (I was
physically standing ~12 blocks from a target I'd walked to earlier the same session), then the
`pf` fallback burns a full 45s per attempt (up to 5 attempts = 225s worst case) before either
succeeding or giving up. My own manual `/eval` walk hit the matching micro-cause: the only floor-
level opening between my shelter's furniture nook and the rest of the room is a genuine 1-wide
diagonal corner squeeze (open cell at 9,*,57 flanked by solid blocks on both straight sides,
birch_log west + oak_log south, nothing open on either full face) — the kind of corner vanilla
movement can't cut through without an axis-aligned approach, which is plausibly also what's
defeating ashfinder's planner. Recommend: (1) ashfinder's reachability check gets a false negative
in tight indoor furniture clusters — worth a minimum repro (this exact shelter, any far outdoor
goal) for Engineer; (2) the pf fallback's 45s-per-attempt is a long silent stretch for a driver
polling normally — a driver hitting this will see many "no progress" polls before the 5-attempt
ladder either resolves or truly fails, don't panic-escalate to wedge-ladder before ~225s elapsed on
a goto that logged this exact ashfinder-fail-then-pf-timeout pair.

input.command:
for i in $(seq 1 8); do
  sleep 15
  st=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3202/status)
  echo "$st" | python3 -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)
t=d['currentTask']
inv=[(i['name'],i['count']) for i in d['inventory'] if i['name'] in ('raw_iron','coal')]
print(f'poll $i: state={t[\"state\"]} kind={t[\"kind\"]} inv={inv}')
if t['state'] in ('done','failed'):
    print(f'TASK_ENDED: {t[\"state\"]} {t.get(\"result\")}')
"
  state=$(echo "$st" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['currentTask']['state'], d['currentTask']['kind'])" 2>/dev/null)
  st2=$(echo "$state" | awk '{print $1}')
  kind=$(echo "$state" | awk '{print $2}')
  if [ "$kind" = "withdraw" ] && { [ "$st2" = "done" ] || [ "$st2" = "failed" ]; }; then
    break
  fi
done

  st=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3202/status)
  echo "$st" | python3 -c "

  kind=$(echo "$state" | awk '{print $2}')
  if [ "$kind" = "smelt" ] && { [ "$st2" = "done" ] || [ "$st2" = "failed" ]; }; then
    break
  fi
done

input.command:
for i in $(seq 1 8); do
  sleep 20
  st=$(curl -s http://127.0.0.1:3202/status)
  echo "$st" | python3 -c "
import json,sys
d=json.load(sys.stdin)
t=d['currentTask']
inv=[(i['name'],i['count']) for i in d['inventory'] if i['name']=='iron_ingot']
print(f'poll $i: state={t[\"state\"]} kind={t[\"kind\"]} inv={inv}')
if t['state'] in ('done','failed'):
    print(f'TASK_ENDED: {t[\"state\"]} {t.get(\"result\")}')
"
  state=$(echo "$st" | python3 -c "import json,sys; d=json.load(sys.stdin); print(d['currentTask']['state'], d['currentTask']['kind'])" 2>/dev/null)
  st2=$(echo "$state" | awk '{print $1}')
  kind=$(echo "$state" | awk '{print $2}')
  if [ "$kind" = "withdraw" ] && { [ "$st2" = "done" ] || [ "$st2" = "failed" ]; }; then
    break
  fi
done

"

  if [ "$state" = "done" ] || [ "$state" = "failed" ]; then
    break
  fi
done
